sets.title: Quick Quiz
sets.description: Test your understanding of Russian word order and emphasis
sets.descriptionRussian: Проверьте понимание порядка слов и выделения в русском языке

items.prompt: Which sentence uses neutral (SVO) word order?
items.promptEnglish: Which sentence uses neutral (SVO) word order?
items.hint: Subject first, then verb, then object.
items.explanation: SVO = Subject (Мама) + Verb (читает) + Object (книгу). This is the neutral, unmarked order.

items.prompt: How do you ask a yes/no question in Russian?
items.promptEnglish: How do you ask a yes/no question in Russian?
items.explanation: Russian forms yes/no questions with rising intonation alone: Ты студент? The word order stays the same.

items.prompt: In the answer to «Кто читает?», where does the new information go?
items.promptEnglish: In the answer to 'Who is reading?', where does the new information go?
items.hint: New or emphasized information has a special position.
items.explanation: New information goes at the END: Книгу читает МАМА. (It's Mom who's reading.)

items.prompt: «Музыку я люблю.» What is emphasized here?
items.hint: The word moved to the front gets emphasis.
items.explanation: Moving the object (Музыку) to the front emphasizes it: It's MUSIC that I love.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Which sentence is in neutral SVO order?
minimalPairs.explanation: SVO (Subject-Verb-Object) is the neutral order. Папа (S) пишет (V) письмо (O).

minimalPairs.context: Which answer emphasizes WHO did it? — Кто готовит ужин?
minimalPairs.explanation: New information (мама) goes at the end to answer 'Who?': Ужин готовит МАМА.

minimalPairs.context: Ты говоришь по-русски? - How is this a question?
minimalPairs.explanation: The word order is the same as a statement. Only the intonation rises to make it a question.

minimalPairs.context: Which emphasizes WHAT she reads? — Что она читает?
minimalPairs.explanation: Moving газету to the front emphasizes it: It's the NEWSPAPER she reads.

sets.title: Fill and Sort
sets.description: Fill in the emphasized word and sort sentences by order type
sets.descriptionRussian: Вставьте выделенное слово и рассортируйте предложения по типу

blanks: — Где живёт Саша? — Саша живёт в _____.
— Кто играет на гитаре? — На гитаре играет _____.
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: new information at the end of answers
hints: The answer to 'Who?' goes at the end.
The answer to 'What?' goes at the front for emphasis.
The answer to 'Where?' goes at the end.
The answer to 'Who?' goes at the end.
explanations: Ужин готовит мама. The new info (мама) answers 'who?' at the end.
Газету я читаю. The object is fronted to emphasize what is being read.
Саша живёт в Москве. The location answers 'where?' at the end.
На гитаре играет брат. The new info (брат) answers 'who?' at the end.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort: neutral SVO or changed for emphasis?

sets.title: Build and Translate
sets.description: Build sentences in the right order and translate emphasis patterns
sets.descriptionRussian: Составьте предложения в правильном порядке и переведите

translation.hint: dad = папа, reads = читает, newspaper = газету
Question by intonation, no word order change
she = она, speaks = говорит, Russian = по-русски

items.promptEnglish: What does Sasha like? Sasha likes _____.
items.hint: The answer to 'what?' is the new information.
items.explanation: Музыку answers 'what does Sasha like?' and goes at the end in neutral order.

items.prompt: Which sentence is a question formed only by intonation?
items.promptEnglish: Which is a question formed only by intonation?
items.explanation: Ты студент? has no question word. It's a yes/no question made by rising intonation alone.

items.promptEnglish: Who writes the letter? _____ writes it.
items.hint: The answer to 'who?' goes at the end.
items.explanation: Брат is the new information answering 'who?' It goes at the end for emphasis.

sets.title: Find the Mistakes
sets.description: Spot word order and emphasis mistakes
sets.descriptionRussian: Найдите ошибки в порядке слов и выделении

items.prompt: — Кто читает книгу? Which answer emphasizes WHO?
items.promptEnglish: Who reads the book? Which answer emphasizes who?
items.hint: New information (who) goes at the end.
items.explanation: To emphasize мама (answering 'who?'), put it at the end: Книгу читает мама.

items.prompt: How does Russian form yes/no questions?
items.promptEnglish: How does Russian form yes/no questions?
items.explanation: Russian uses rising intonation alone for yes/no questions. No 'do' or word-order change.

items.prompt: — Что ты пьёшь? Which answer emphasizes TEA?
items.promptEnglish: What are you drinking? Which emphasizes tea?
items.hint: Move the emphasized word to the front.
items.explanation: Fronting the object emphasizes it: Чай я пью. (It's TEA I'm drinking.)

items.prompt: Which word order answers «Что делает мама?» most naturally?
items.promptEnglish: Which answers 'What is mom doing?' most naturally?
items.hint: The answer to 'what is she doing?' keeps neutral order.
items.explanation: The question asks about the action, so neutral SVO works: Мама готовит ужин.

items.prompt: «Он живёт в Москве.» Is this a statement or a question?
items.promptEnglish: Is this a statement or a question?
items.explanation: With falling intonation it's a statement. With rising intonation (Он живёт в Москве?) it's a question. Word order stays the same.

items.hint: The answer to 'who?' goes at the end.
items.explanation: Сестра answers 'who?' The new information is placed at the end for emphasis.

items.prompt: Which emphasizes that it's COFFEE (not tea) she drinks?
items.hint: Move the emphasized word to the front.
items.explanation: Fronting the object emphasizes it: Кофе она пьёт. (It's COFFEE she drinks.)

sets.title: Mixed Challenge
sets.description: A fresh round mixing all word order skills
sets.descriptionRussian: Новый раунд по всем темам порядка слов

items.prompt: Which is the neutral order for 'Sister writes a letter'?
items.promptEnglish: Which is the neutral SVO order?
items.hint: Subject first, verb second, object third.

items.prompt: «Ты любишь кофе?» How is this question formed?
items.hint: No question word, no word order change.
items.explanation: This is a yes/no question formed by intonation alone. The word order is identical to a statement.

items.promptEnglish: Who is making soup? _____ is making it.
items.hint: New information answering 'who?' goes at the end.
items.explanation: Бабушка answers 'who?' and is placed at the end: Суп варит бабушка.

patternRecognition.prompt: What do «Книгу читает мама», «Суп готовит папа», and «Письмо пишет брат» have in common?
options: The object is first and the subject is last for emphasis
patternRecognition.answer: The object is first and the subject is last for emphasis
patternRecognition.explanation: All three move the object to the front and place the subject (new info) at the end for emphasis.

patternRecognition.prompt: What do «Ты студент?», «Он работает?», and «Она говорит по-русски?» have in common?
options: They change word order to form questions
They are yes/no questions formed by intonation
patternRecognition.answer: They are yes/no questions formed by intonation
patternRecognition.explanation: None of these have question words. They are all yes/no questions made by raising the intonation.
